title: Dividing algebraic expressions

steps.title: Separate coefficient and variable
steps.action: Make three equal groups of the twelve coefficient units; keep x in each group.
steps.narration: Only the coefficient is shared into three groups.

steps.title: Count one group
steps.action: Twelve divided by three is four.
steps.narration: Each group contains four x, so the quotient is four x.

worked_examples.repair: Keep the variable attached to each equal group.

steps.title: Carry the sign
steps.action: Place negative fifteen over positive five without changing the sign.
steps.narration: A negative dividend divided by a positive number stays negative.

steps.title: Share the magnitude
steps.action: Divide fifteen by five and retain a.
steps.narration: Three a remains negative.

worked_examples.repair: Check the signs before sharing the coefficient.

steps.title: Split factors
steps.action: Divide eighteen by six and cancel exactly one x from x times x, provided x is nonzero.
steps.narration: The divisor contains x, so zero is excluded.

steps.title: Count factors left
steps.action: Three remains with one x.
steps.narration: One x factor survives, giving three x.

worked_examples.verify: At x=2: 72 ÷ 12=6 and 3(2)=6; x=0 is excluded.
worked_examples.repair: Cross out only one numerator x for the one divisor x.

worked_examples.skill: Divide both terms by an integer

steps.title: Create two quotient lanes
steps.action: Copy the divisor four under eight x and under twelve.
steps.narration: Each signed term needs its own division path.

steps.title: Divide the variable term
steps.action: Eight x divided by four is two x.
steps.narration: Keep the second quotient visible for the next step.

steps.title: Divide the constant
steps.action: Twelve divided by four is three.
steps.narration: Two x plus three is the complete answer.

worked_examples.repair: Draw a separate path from four to each bracket term.

worked_examples.skill: Divide a binomial by a monomial

steps.title: Split the numerator
steps.action: Place six x under both signed terms, with x nonzero.
steps.narration: The denominator acts on both terms.

steps.title: Cancel the first term
steps.action: Twelve divided by six is two; x squared divided by x leaves x.
steps.narration: The first quotient is two x.

steps.title: Cancel the second term
steps.action: Eighteen divided by six is three; x divided by x is one.
steps.narration: The second quotient is three, not three x.

worked_examples.misconception: Leaving an x on the second quotient.
worked_examples.repair: Match each numerator x with one divisor x.

worked_examples.skill: Divide signed terms by a negative

steps.title: Preserve term signs
steps.action: Copy negative eight beneath negative sixteen a and positive twenty four.
steps.narration: Each quotient has its own sign pair.

steps.title: Resolve double negative
steps.action: Negative sixteen a divided by negative eight is positive two a.
steps.narration: Two negatives make a positive first result.

steps.title: Resolve positive over negative
steps.action: Positive twenty four divided by negative eight is negative three.
steps.narration: The second result is negative three.

worked_examples.misconception: Treating both resulting signs as positive.
worked_examples.repair: Check each dividend and divisor pair separately.

steps.title: Make three quotient lanes
steps.action: Send five to the square, linear and constant terms.
steps.narration: A trinomial needs three division paths.

steps.title: Divide the square term
steps.action: Fifteen x squared divided by five is three x squared.
steps.narration: The x squared factor remains.

steps.title: Divide the negative term
steps.action: Negative ten x divided by five is negative two x.
steps.narration: The second signed result stays negative.

steps.title: Divide the constant
steps.action: Five divided by five is one.
steps.narration: The complete result has three unlike terms.

worked_examples.repair: Count three input terms and three separate quotients.

steps.title: Separate every quotient
steps.action: Write one six p divisor for each signed term, provided p is nonzero.
steps.narration: The shared divisor does not disappear from later terms.

steps.title: Reduce cubic term
steps.action: Twenty four over six is four; three p factors over one leave two.
steps.narration: The first quotient is four p squared.

steps.title: Reduce square term
steps.action: Negative twelve over six is negative two; two p factors over one leave one.
steps.narration: The second quotient is negative two p.

steps.title: Reduce last term
steps.action: Six p divided by six p is one.
steps.narration: The last quotient is one, not p.

worked_examples.misconception: Subtracting exponents from only the first term.
worked_examples.repair: Make a factor cancellation lane for every term.

worked_examples.skill: Cancel a shared letter, retain another

steps.title: Give each term a divisor
steps.action: Place six a under eighteen a b and under negative twelve a.
steps.narration: A is cancelled only because it is a nonzero common factor.

steps.title: Keep b in first result
steps.action: Eighteen over six is three; the a pair cancels, leaving b.
steps.narration: The first quotient is three b.

steps.title: Resolve the signed constant
steps.action: Negative twelve over six is negative two; cancel the a pair.
steps.narration: The second quotient is negative two.

worked_examples.misconception: Cancelling b even though it is absent from the divisor.

steps.title: Mark the excluded input
steps.action: Since x is the divisor, x cannot equal zero; split the two terms.
steps.narration: A quotient cannot have a zero denominator.

steps.title: Cancel the square term
steps.action: One x factor cancels from x times x.
steps.narration: One x survives in the first quotient.

steps.title: Cancel the second term
steps.action: Five x over x leaves five.
steps.narration: The result x plus five retains the original exclusion.

worked_examples.verify: At x=2: (4+10) ÷ 2=7 and 2+5=7; x=0 is undefined in the original.
worked_examples.misconception: Claiming x=0 is allowed because the simplified form has no fraction.
worked_examples.repair: Carry the original domain restriction into the answer.

worked_examples.q: Six identical packs contain 24x + 12 counters altogether. Write an expression for the counters in one pack.

steps.title: Draw six equal packs
steps.action: Split both twenty four x and twelve across the six packs.
steps.narration: Each pack receives a share of both kinds of counters.

steps.title: Share the x counters
steps.action: Twenty four x divided into six packs is four x per pack.
steps.narration: Each pack gets four x counters.

steps.title: Share the loose counters
steps.action: Twelve divided by six is two.
steps.narration: Each pack contains four x plus two counters.

worked_examples.repair: Show both types repeated in each of six packs.

worked_examples.q: A learner writes (12x + 8) ÷ 4 = 3x + 8. Find the first mistake and correct it.
states: Both 12x and 8 must be divided by 4

steps.title: Trace both paths
steps.action: Inspect the written three x and eight against the two required quotient lanes.
steps.narration: The first term is divided; the second is merely copied.

steps.title: Check first quotient
steps.action: Twelve x over four is three x.
steps.narration: The first part of the learner answer is correct.

steps.title: Find the first error
steps.action: Eight over four is two, not eight.
steps.narration: The error begins at the unchanged constant.

steps.title: Replace the wrong constant
steps.action: Keep three x and replace eight by two.
steps.narration: The repaired result is three x plus two.

worked_examples.verify: At x=1: original 20 ÷ 4=5, wrong claim 11, corrected 3+2=5.
worked_examples.misconception: Accepting the first correct term as proof of the whole answer.
worked_examples.repair: Check each signed term against its own denominator.

steps.title: Give both terms the signed divisor
steps.action: Write negative three x under each signed numerator term; x is nonzero.
steps.narration: The same negative divisor changes each quotient sign separately.

steps.title: Reduce positive over negative
steps.action: Six over negative three is negative two; x squared over x is x.
steps.narration: The first result is negative two x.

steps.title: Reduce negative over negative
steps.action: Negative nine x over negative three x is positive three.
steps.narration: The second result is positive three.

worked_examples.repair: Use a sign pair for each term, then cancel factors.

steps.title: Finish first quotient
steps.action: Divide both eighteen x squared and twelve x by six x.
steps.narration: The first bracket becomes three x plus two.

steps.title: Finish second quotient
steps.action: Divide both eight x and four by four.
steps.narration: The second bracket becomes two x plus one.

steps.title: Subtract the whole second result
steps.action: Change both signs in the second bracket before collecting.
steps.narration: Subtracting two x plus one means subtracting two x and one.

steps.title: Collect like terms
steps.action: Three x minus two x is x; two minus one is one.
steps.narration: The result is x plus one with x still nonzero.

worked_examples.misconception: Subtracting only 2x and retaining positive one.
worked_examples.repair: Put a subtraction badge on both terms of the second quotient.

worked_examples.skill: Three powers over a common monomial

steps.title: Make three factor lanes
steps.action: Put six x beneath every signed numerator term, excluding x=0.
steps.narration: The shared denominator reaches all three terms.

steps.title: Cancel a cubic factor
steps.action: Twelve over six is two; three x factors over one leave two.
steps.narration: The first quotient is two x squared.

steps.title: Cancel a square factor
steps.action: Negative eighteen over six is negative three; two x factors over one leave one.
steps.narration: The second quotient is negative three x.

steps.title: Reduce the final term
steps.action: Six x divided by six x is one.
steps.narration: The final constant is one, while x=0 stays excluded.

worked_examples.misconception: Keeping x on the last quotient or losing the restriction.
worked_examples.repair: Cancel equal factors one lane at a time and preserve the original domain.

practice_questions: Subtract one exponent in each lane.
Five identical packs contain 15x + 10 counters. Express one pack.
Share both types among five packs.
Subtract both terms of the second quotient.
Keep the term signs and zero exclusion.
mastery_questions: x - 1, where x ≠ 0; at x=2 both forms equal 1.
reassessment_questions: x, where x ≠ 0; at x=2 both forms equal 2.
